test_cases.requirement: Every pre-acquisition authentication, validation, authorization, resource-reference, expiry and material-mismatch variant has an independently sourced exact application/HTTP denial and durable fail-closed oracle.
test_cases.risk: An omitted denial branch can acquire execution, approval can be mistaken for execution authority, or stale approval can silently become reusable.
prerequisites: one approved proposal per literal pre-acquisition fixture row
independent literal matrix and digest importing no production result type, error mapper, serializer or HTTP mapper
missing/invalid authentication plus malformed/non-object JSON, revision-shape and forbidden-identity-field fixtures
path/current Workspace, resource and read/observation/execution authority matrix
capability/binding/policy mutation adapters plus immutable target/reference substitution fixture
named workflow, proposal-lookup, acquisition, admission, execution-start/terminal-audit, gateway, target-lookup and provider sentinels
steps: Load the independent fixture and seed a separate approved proposal, direct durable before snapshot and named sentinel set for every row.

Exercise separate rows for missing and invalid authentication; malformed and non-object JSON; missing, non-integer or boolean expected_revision; extra logical_execution_id and request_fingerprint; path and current Workspace denial; resource denial; no execution, read-only, observation-only and read-plus-observation grants; capability, binding and policy identity/version/digest mismatch; malformed and non-canonical m4r1; MAC, protected-claim and protected-scope corruption; trusted-store delete/replacement/claims-mismatch/unavailable; revoked/unknown key; expired resource reference; and proposal expiry.
Compare every directly representable application outcome and decoded HTTP status/body/key set with its literal row, then reload durable state and capture every named sentinel count.

Restore only conditions the approved design classifies as temporary and retry the same approval; separately restore each material capability/binding/policy selector and retry the invalidated old approval; reject immutable target/reference substitution without inventing a reference CompatibilityReason, and prove malformed, scope-mismatched, revoked or expired references cannot regain executability from preserved provenance.
expected_results: Each application/transport denial and HTTP status/body equals the exact independent literal row; the body has only error.code and never contains status.

Every denial creates zero execution, acquisition, admission, execution-start audit and terminal-audit artifacts and zero gateway, target-lookup and provider calls for named sentinels; authentication, path-Workspace and raw HTTP-validation rows additionally have zero proposal lookups and workflow calls.

Temporary Workspace/resource/execution denial and every m4r1 syntax/integrity/scope/trust/key/expiry denial preserve exact immutable approved proposal and approval provenance; an attempted material target/reference replacement is rejected by the immutable command/persistence boundary, creates no compatibility reason, and a different target requires a new proposal plus authorized-human approval.
Proposal expiry preserves approval identity/version/digest while projecting approved, non-stale, non-executable and expired; there is no separate approval-expiry state.
Each capability/binding/policy mismatch persists its exact typed stale/invalidated state and requires a new proposal and human approval even after the old selector is restored.
evidence_to_capture: independent literal matrix source/digest and one release-evidence record per physical row
exact application/HTTP result and recursive key-set comparison per row
before/after durable proposal and approval snapshot digests
old-approval retry result for temporary and capability/binding/policy material rows
immutable target/reference substitution rejection and new-proposal/new-authorized-human-approval provenance

test_cases.requirement: Logical execution identity and canonical request fingerprint are server-owned, immutable and acquired atomically by one contender.
test_cases.risk: Caller influence, partial acquisition, or losing contenders can create duplicate provider paths.
test_cases.seam: application/HTTP schema, canonicalizer, PostgreSQL acquisition CAS and concurrent public workflow
prerequisites: independent acquisition-witness field list and restart projector
steps: Inject logical ID/fingerprint fields through application and HTTP inputs.

Independently recompute the fingerprint from server-normalized operation, exact capability, scope, protected reference/resource claims and normalized {title, description}; compare the fingerprint and server-minted logical ID at proposal, complete AcquireWitness, admission, persisted envelope and provider verification boundaries.
Race identified contenders, read the committed acquisition tuple after commit and restart, inspect a separate session before commit, and inject faults after each acquisition write before commit.
expected_results: Identity injection is rejected before state creation.
Server identities are not caller-selectable or caller-influenceable, are byte-identical at every boundary and remain immutable after restart.

Exactly one AcquireApplied contender commits one complete generation-1 AcquireWitness tuple; every loser makes zero gateway/provider calls, pre-commit visibility is empty and each rollback leaves no execution, snapshot, audit fragment or caller-influenced identity.
evidence_to_capture: canonical input/digest comparison at all proposal/acquisition/admission/envelope/provider boundaries
complete acquisition tuple and post-restart reconstruction

test_cases.requirement: Admission revalidates current authority, compatibility and complete m4r1 state under locks, and every post-acquisition denial has an exact application/HTTP projection with independently sourced durable identities.
test_cases.risk: TOCTOU changes can authorize stale dispatch, escape the closed public-result/error contract, or substitute incorrect proposal/execution identities.
test_cases.seam: private authorize_and_admit_dispatch with real mutation and non-runtime integrity adapters
prerequisites: pre-invocation scenario identity authority from independent seed plus direct durable proposal/acquisition reload
explicit compatible, active, retiring, revoked, unknown, unavailable and rotation-transition fixtures
same-transaction mutation/epoch witnesses with rollback branches
static-registry identity/version/digest reload fixture and mutable-source ineligibility probe
production application/HTTP composition and request-selector negative probes
steps: Acquire and block before admission.

Run every post-acquisition denial-matrix row: Workspace/resource/execution authority; capability/binding/policy identity, version and digest; canonical bytes, MAC, protected claims and protected-scope corruption; trusted-store delete, replacement and claims mismatch; revoked, unknown and unavailable key state; reference expiry; and retiring-to-revoked mutation-first.
Run compatible, active exact, retiring exact, active-to-retiring and admission-first controls.

For every supported Workspace-owned authority/selector mutation and each reference-key mutation, capture the changed authoritative row plus exactly one corresponding epoch increment under one transaction/commit marker, then run and record a rollback branch.

Capture the dual-scope mutation lock order (global reference-key epoch then Workspace) and admission lock order (execution row then global reference-key epoch then Workspace); reload the compiled static registry across process/restart and attempt mutable-source, registration and request-controlled signer/mutator/provider selections.

Before every denial invocation, capture expected proposal and generation-1 logical execution identities from independent seed authority and direct durable reload; compare those identities, private denial, ProposalNotExecutable projection and decoded HTTP status/body with the independently loaded exact row before inspecting post-lock epochs, persistence and calls.
expected_results: Every denial occurs after canonical admission locks and equals one exact independently sourced denial row.
Each denial application projection has exactly proposal_id, logical_execution_id, lifecycle=executing, outcome_type=proposal_not_executable and the row's exact reason_code.

For every denial row, both IDs are canonical lowercase RFC 4122 UUIDs and exactly equal independently seeded/directly reloaded durable proposal and generation-1 acquisition identities; expected values are never derived from the returned projection or production mapper.
Each denial HTTP response has the row's exact 400/403/409 status and exactly {error:{code:<PUBLIC_CODE>}}, with no other outer or nested field.

Every denial persists zero DispatchAdmissionWitness/admission-audit rows and makes zero gateway/provider calls; protected-scope corruption and reference expiry map to resource_access_denied plus 403/TOOL_RESOURCE_ACCESS_DENIED using fresh post-lock PostgreSQL time.

Each mutation witness binds the changed row and exactly one epoch increment to one transaction/commit marker; rollback leaves both unchanged. Dual-scope and admission lock orders are exact, inverse/alternate order is rejected, and compatible active/retiring controls admit once under epoch linearization.

The static registry exposes immutable registry_identity/version/digest equal across process/restart, has no plugin/dynamic epoch, and registration/mutation or mutable authorization-source attempts cannot authorize dispatch; production composition cannot resolve test-only adapters and request-controlled selectors are rejected before state. Evidence remains sanitized.
evidence_to_capture: per-row durable identity source references and expected/actual proposal_id and logical_execution_id equality
per-mutation transaction/commit marker, pre/post row and epoch values and rollback absence
execution-to-global-to-Workspace admission lock trace and global-to-Workspace dual-mutation trace
static-registry identity/version/digest across process/restart and mutable-source ineligibility result
production DI/resolver and request-selector negative probes

test_cases.requirement: Epoch locks and fresh post-lock PostgreSQL time linearize mutation, admission and expiry.
test_cases.risk: Lock-order gaps, stale transaction time or concurrent issuers can mint an unauthorized admission.
test_cases.seam: PostgreSQL execution/global-key/Workspace-epoch transactions and deterministic lock barriers
prerequisites: compiled static-registry reload and mutable-source probe
steps: Race each real typed Workspace authority/resource/execution/capability/binding/policy mutation and reference-key mutation against admission, and race concurrent same-generation issuers.
For every mutation capture the changed authoritative row and exactly one epoch increment in the same transaction/commit marker, then inject rollback and verify both remain unchanged.

Exercise dual-scope mutation with global reference-key then Workspace locking and deliberately attempt inverse order; capture admission execution-row then global reference-key epoch then Workspace locking and reject alternate order.

Block acquisition across proposal expiry and admission across reference and lease expiry under skewed non-database clocks; reload the static registry across process/restart and attempt mutable runtime/request/provider-discovery sources.
expected_results: Mutation-first denies and admission-first binds the exact prior epoch vector; one byte-identical admission/audit record exists.

Every Workspace-owned mutation advances workspace_dispatch_epoch exactly once with its row under one commit marker; every reference-key mutation advances reference_key_epoch exactly once; rollback leaves both unchanged.

Dual-scope mutation order is global reference-key epoch then Workspace and admission order is execution then global then Workspace; inverse/alternate order is rejected with no admission/provider call.
Static registry identity/version/digest is immutable and equal across reload with no plugin epoch; mutable sources are ineligible and cannot authorize dispatch.

Fresh post-lock clock_timestamp decides proposal, reference and lease boundaries; skewed or transaction-start clocks cannot revive them. Admission-side reference expiry uses the exact TC-03 resource_access_denied / 403 TOOL_RESOURCE_ACCESS_DENIED row and zero-activity evidence.
evidence_to_capture: same-transaction row/epoch commit-marker traces and rollback absence
dual-mutation global-to-Workspace and admission execution-to-global-to-Workspace lock traces
static-registry reload/mutation and mutable-source ineligibility evidence

expected_results: For admission_schema_version, admission_identity, admission_digest, purpose, workspace_id, proposal_id, logical_execution_id, request_fingerprint, capability_identity, capability_version, capability_digest, binding_identity, binding_version, binding_digest, policy_identity, policy_version, policy_digest, reference_identity, reference_version, reference_digest, reference_claims_digest, resource_identity_digest, canonical_target_digest, canonical_parameter_digest, complete_intent_digest, reference_key_epoch, workspace_dispatch_epoch, authority_decision_digest, authority_witness_digest, owner, generation, database_issue_time, lease_started_at, lease_deadline, envelope_signing_key_identity, envelope_signing_key_version, routing_snapshot_digest, canonical_envelope_digest, admission_audit_identity and admission_audit_digest, the persisted value is individually non-null and exactly equal to its authoritative expected value.

Committed readback returns exactly one complete tuple whose individual field values, canonical tuple bytes/digest and private envelope bytes are byte-identical to the intended values after restart/key rotation; no second insert, audit, claim set, signing operation or envelope regeneration occurs.

test_cases.requirement: Admission-first dispatch cannot be canceled, upgraded or retargeted by later authority/config/key changes or expiry.
test_cases.risk: A started external write can be silently altered or canceled after approval/admission.
steps: Pause immediately after admission commit.
Independently mutate/revoke each current fact and cross every expiry boundary.
Resume dispatch and inspect exact gateway input.
expected_results: Exactly one call carries the original byte-identical envelope and intent.
No reauthorization, cancellation, replacement, key upgrade or retarget occurs.
Later lease expiry may fence only Knora observation/finalization.

test_cases.requirement: The independent SQLite provider atomically owns effects, closed outcomes and idempotency conflicts and rejects cross-binding before resource access.
test_cases.risk: Provider replay/conflict/cross-binding bugs or non-atomic rejection persistence can duplicate, retarget or lose external truth.

production application/HTTP DI manifest and request-selector rejection probes

Exercise same-ID/same-fingerprint replay and two independently valid same-ID/different-fingerprint requests.
Exercise ordinary tampering and, as a separate row, deliver an integrity-valid envelope bound to a different Workspace/external-scope binding than the selected provider target.
Capture ordered provider verification, target-lookup, SQLite transaction/ledger and effect sentinels for both negative rows.
Parameterize success and all three closed rejections with pre-commit and post-commit-before-ack faults, then reopen SQLite.

Ordinary tampering rejects before SQLite mutation.

Each closed rejection owns one exact durable ledger row, zero effects, rollback absence and restart-stable replay.

test_cases.requirement: Generation-1 observation/finalization uses fresh post-lock PostgreSQL time, is lease-fenced, and every execution outcome or post-acquisition denial uses a complete immutable sanitized application/HTTP matrix with independently sourced identities.
test_cases.risk: Expired owners can finalize provider truth using stale clocks, denial identities can be substituted, or public projections can leak private admission material.
test_cases.seam: distinct PostgreSQL observation/finalization execution-row lock barriers plus independently loaded execution-outcome and post-acquisition-denial application/HTTP matrices
prerequisites: provider-only success and three closed outcomes
separate observation and finalization fixtures with distinct execution-row lock barriers
operation-start, PostgreSQL transaction-time and fresh post-lock clock_timestamp capture
before-expiry controls on the same observation/finalization paths
ordered append-only observation and audit projections
immutable execution-outcome matrix loaded independently from production serializers
immutable post-acquisition denial application/HTTP matrix with pre-invocation durable identity authority
before-result, after-result and post-PostgreSQL-restart snapshots for every non-finalizing matrix row
terminal outcome/finalization row, terminal-audit append and operation-correlated finalization-write counters
steps: For provider-only success and every closed rejection, prepare separate observation fixtures with no PostgreSQL observation and finalization fixtures with one durable authorized observation ready to finalize; begin each operation before lease_expires_at, record operation start and PostgreSQL transaction timestamp, skew application/non-database clocks and block behind the governing execution-row lock before the expiry decision.

While each operation is blocked, use an independent PostgreSQL session to prove clock_timestamp() is later than lease_expires_at, release the lock, capture the operation's own fresh clock_timestamp() immediately after lock acquisition, invoke the operation and capture before/after execution, observation, audit and operation-correlated write projections.

Repeat the same observation and finalization paths as before-expiry controls, releasing while both independent and operation post-lock PostgreSQL times remain before lease_expires_at. Link, without republishing, the provider-boundary-only read-only provider_outcome_not_found evidence from TC-08; do not invoke or add an application/HTTP projection for it. Then exercise the public indeterminate, current in-progress, provider-conflict and fenced result rows.

For ExecutionIndeterminate, current ExecutionInProgress, provider-conflict ExecutionInProgress, ExecutionFenced and every post-acquisition ProposalNotExecutable row, capture operation-correlated before, after and post-PostgreSQL-restart execution/finalization/terminal-audit snapshots and link provider conflict to the exact TC-07 record.

Before every TC-03 denial invocation, capture expected proposal and generation-1 logical execution identities from independent seed authority and direct durable reload, then invoke application and HTTP seams.

For every row in both independent matrices, compare exact application result, outcome_type, lifecycle, HTTP status, complete key sets and value domains including denial identity equality; recursively inject forbidden fields.
expected_results: For observation and finalization independently, each expired branch starts and establishes its transaction timestamp before the deadline, samples fresh PostgreSQL time after lock acquisition later than the deadline, returns ExecutionFenced and appends zero operation-correlated execution/observation/audit or other PostgreSQL writes.

Each valid-lease before-expiry control samples fresh post-lock PostgreSQL time before the deadline: success records one durable observation/audit and finalizes to succeeded with the exact success outcome; target_not_found, validation_rejected and policy_rejected each record one durable observation/audit and finalize to failed with its exact rejection_code and zero target effects. Skewed application/non-database and transaction-start clocks decide neither branch.

Every application/HTTP execution outcome exactly matches one execution-outcome row, including status, lifecycle, fields and value domains. provider_outcome_not_found exists only as the linked TC-08 private provider-boundary read-only observation, has no #77 application/HTTP projection or public matrix row, and grants no retry authority. indeterminate_external_outcome and provider fingerprint conflict never terminalize.

Every TC-03 denial exactly matches one ProposalNotExecutable application row and one closed HTTP error-envelope row, and both IDs are canonical lowercase RFC 4122 UUIDs exactly equal pre-invocation independently seeded/directly reloaded durable identities; no denial remains unclassified.
Application denial fields are exactly proposal_id, logical_execution_id, lifecycle, outcome_type and reason_code; HTTP denial fields are exactly error.code.
The expected matrices import or call no production result type, enum, serializer or HTTP mapper.
Provider truth survives restart and every extra/private-field injection fails closed.

Every admitted non-terminal fixture remains generation 1 and executing after PostgreSQL restart with unchanged proposal_id, logical_execution_id, request_fingerprint and admission_identity; this applies to indeterminate_external_outcome, the admitted current-execution fixture, provider fingerprint conflict and the post-admission fenced fixture.

Protected-scope corruption and reference expiry are post-acquisition but pre-admission denials: after PostgreSQL restart each retains unchanged proposal_id, logical_execution_id, request_fingerprint, generation and acquisition witness/audit identity, while DispatchAdmissionWitness row count and admission-audit row count remain zero. No admission_identity exists or is asserted for either denial.

For every non-finalizing application/HTTP row and the separately linked provider-boundary-only observation, terminal outcome/finalization row count, terminal-audit append delta and operation-correlated finalization-write count are zero and the terminal-column/row-set digest is unchanged.

Provider conflict has exactly proposal_id, logical_execution_id, lifecycle=executing, outcome_type=execution_in_progress and reason_code=provider_idempotency_conflict in both the application projection and decoded HTTP 409 body, while TC-07 retains one original provider ledger/effect and no second effect.
Typed non-terminal observation or audit activity is counted separately and does not violate the terminal-write oracle.
evidence_to_capture: separate observation/finalization clock tuples with lease deadline, operation start, transaction timestamp, skewed application clocks, blocker/release/lock-acquisition ordering, independent boundary sample and deciding post-lock clock_timestamp
expired and before-expiry PostgreSQL state/row-set digests and operation-correlated write counts

per-admitted-non-terminal-row before/after/post-restart generation, lifecycle, proposal/logical/fingerprint/admission identity, terminal-row, terminal-audit, finalization-write and terminal-digest comparisons
protected-scope and reference-expiry pre-admission before/after/post-restart acquisition-identity equality plus exact zero admission/admission-audit counts
TC-08 provider-boundary-only provider_outcome_not_found linkage with explicit absence from application/HTTP matrices
independent execution and denial matrix sources/digests, including protected-scope and reference-expiry rows
per-row durable identity source references and expected/actual proposal_id and logical_execution_id equality

test_cases.requirement: Append-only PostgreSQL audit reconstructs complete provenance after independent PostgreSQL and SQLite restarts without secrets.
test_cases.risk: Audit omissions or provider-state coupling can destroy provenance or leak private material.
test_cases.seam: PostgreSQL audit projection and independently reopened SQLite provider
prerequisites: direct success/failure, indeterminate, conflict and no-admission fixtures
steps: Restart PostgreSQL and SQLite independently.
Reconstruct audit solely from append-only PostgreSQL records and compare every required field.
Read provider ledger independently and scan audit/public evidence for forbidden values.
expected_results: Audit exactly reconstructs all actors, decisions, compatibility, acquisition/admission witnesses, epochs, times, provider alias, immutable intent/identity/fingerprint, observations and outcome.
Provider ledger remains independently authoritative.
No raw provider/routing, envelope/MAC, key, credential or authority secret appears.

test_cases.requirement: The exact candidate passes focused M4.3, closed static-registry and production-isolation boundaries, full regression, Ruff, Compose and clean Alembic verification.
test_cases.risk: Narrow execution tests can hide dynamic plugin/discovery seams, production-resolvable test signers/mutators, schema/integration faults or M1-M3 regressions.
test_cases.seam: production application/HTTP dependency composition plus governed repository verification on a clean worktree
prerequisites: every production application factory/dependency provider and HTTP dependency/override surface
steps: Instantiate every production application and HTTP composition entrypoint, enumerate the registry through its public typed resolver/descriptor projection and compare the exact ordered capability ID/version/operation set with the closed allowlist.

For each production application factory, dependency provider, HTTP dependency map and override/resolution surface, attempt to resolve by dependency role and by concrete type every test-only m4r1 signer, dispatch-envelope signer, trusted-store mutator, Workspace/resource/execution-authority mutator, capability/binding/policy selector mutator, reference-key mutator and provider-contract-harness signer/mutator.

Attempt invocation only if any probe unexpectedly returns an object, while counting registry, PostgreSQL, SQLite-ledger, target-lookup, provider-call and effect state before/after; any returned callable is a test failure even when invocation itself rejects.

Attempt request-controlled provider/signer/adapter/harness selection, then attempt runtime capability/provider registration, capability/provider discovery and plugin loading through every production application/HTTP composition surface; do not use file-name or source-text inspection as the oracle.
Run the locked focused M4.3 command, recreate/migrate PostgreSQL and run the authoritative full suite serially, then run Ruff, Compose config, clean migration/current checks and inspect Git status.
expected_results: The production registry equals the exact closed typed allowlist and exposes no registration, discovery or plugin-loading operation; the production provider binding is fixed, request-controlled selections are rejected before state/provider activity, and all probes are structurally unavailable or return the production composition's typed unsupported-dependency result.
Every test-only signer/mutator resolution probe returns no object and no callable across every application/HTTP surface; therefore no test-only adapter can be invoked from production composition.

All registration/discovery/plugin and signer/mutator probes leave the registry projection, dependency graph, PostgreSQL state, SQLite ledger, target-lookup count, provider-call count and effect count byte-for-byte/count-for-count unchanged.
All commands exit zero and focused evidence covers TC-01 through TC-11 plus the closed-registry and test-adapter-isolation boundaries.
M1-M3 regressions remain green.
Alembic is at head and the candidate worktree is clean.
evidence_to_capture: production registry projection and allowlist comparison
